nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, can the source mug be identified in the edit, and where is that same mug relative to the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Assess the mug visible in the source, tracking its identity across the edit using visual features and scene context. Complete only if that same mug is to the right of the headphones in the edited image. Partial only if evidence establishes that the source mug itself moved toward the right but did not reach the right side. Absent if the source mug is identifiable and shows no progress toward the right. Unknown if identity or displacement cannot be established; do not count a newly added or duplicated mug on the right as progress.
nodes.binding: Compare the source image's blue mug with the edited image and the headphones; determine whether the source mug itself is identifiable and its displacement relative to the headphones.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
